answer: Archive custody ties each identity to real storage. At minting, one unique archive shard is docked to that name in the wharf index; any node may demand the exact chunk, served within thirty seconds, and three failed serves burn the 12,000 POA bond. A fake needs 10 GB of distinct disk plus its bond, so a hundred clones lock 1.2 million POA and a terabyte before earning, while honest operators serve from their own terrace of drives and each alias on the ridge pays the same.
